verdicts.reason: A: the jar is a reasonable size but its SOLSTICE label is tiny, the jar is pushed up against the decorative circle in the top-left, and SHOP SOLSTICE sits squeezed toward the right edge, a little above the headline's centre line. B: the jar is shrunk even more, so its label is unreadable and the sun icon is just a speck, and the jar is jammed under the circle, which leaves a big empty gap between the jar and the headline.

The two are almost the same left-to-right banner. In A the jar's green knob touches the decorative circle, and the CTA is only about 14px from the right edge. B moves the jar off the circle and gives the CTA a slightly wider right margin. Both still have a tiny, hard-to-read jar label and a small CTA that looks disconnected from the headline.

A flips the reading order: SHOP SOLSTICE comes first on the left, before the headline, with the jar on the far right, so the call to action reads before the message, and the CTA crowds the circle. B keeps the original order, but the jar is shrunk too far: the label can't be read, the sun is reduced to a dot, and the jar sits tight against the circle.

A keeps the original order (jar, then headline, then CTA) with decent spacing, though the jar label is tiny and the CTA is small and floats on its own. B puts SHOP SOLSTICE ahead of the headline on the left, breaking the brand-to-message-to-action order, and pushes the product to the far right.
